title: Man with axe rushed cops, inquest hears
article: A patron of Taps Tavern who saw a 46-year-old Cambodian refugee shot and killed by Hamilton police told the province's Special Investigations Unit the two officers had no choice but to shoot the disturbed man.
Frank Curto, who was having a cigarette outside the Parkdale Avenue North tavern at about 2:15 a.m. on April 6, 2007, said he saw Soun Saing enter the building and head upstairs to M & J Billiards.

Curto said he spoke to the stranger, who glared at him but did not say a word. A short time later, a police cruiser pulled up to the front and two officers got out and began shouting at Saing, who had reappeared, to "drop the axe."
The investigation by the SIU would later absolve Hamilton police constables Ryan James and Ryan Tocher, who opened fire on Saing after he lunged at them with a hatchet and a knife.
The two patrol officers had been nearby on Ottawa Street North when they received a dispatch about the pool hall owner being struck in the forehead by a man wielding a hatchet.
Curto did not testify in person at the opening of a coroner's inquest yesterday, but a DVD of his statement to the SIU was played for Dr. John Carlisle and the coroner's jury.

Coroner's counsel Karen Shea provided a transcript for the three-man, two-woman jury whose task it will be to establish how, why and by what means Saing was killed and to perhaps make recommendations on how to prevent other deaths in similar circumstances.

Curto said Saing raised the hatchet in the air in a threatening fashion and then "sprinted" toward one of the officers. "He had no choice but to shoot him because the man was coming at him with an axe," he said.
The witness said he was amazed by Saing's extraordinary strength to continue running after being hit by one bullet and then another. Curto said he suspected the man was on drugs.
"He wasn't going to jail, let's put it that way," he told the SIU. "He was going to kill the officer. He wasn't just going to run past him... He was going to hit him with that axe."
SIU forensic investigator Karl Radix testified about finding the hatchet and large knife on the sidewalk outside the tavern.

Radix said six spent cartridges were found on street. Two projectiles were lodged in the body of the deceased, one in the doorway of a nearby barber shop and another in a storage box on the tavern patio.
Hamilton lawyer Graydon Sheppard, representing the deceased's widow and children, asked Radix to account for the missing projectiles.
"That's hard to say," replied Radix. He said projectile fragments were found on the sidewalk, which meant one or both had broken up on impact with the concrete.
